Arizona Cardinals.longComment: After Allgeier sat out Wednesday's session due to a toe injury, his ability to mix into drills one day later generally is a good sign as the Cardinals go through Week 8 prep. Friday's practice report will unveil if Allgeier enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, and also whether or not rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has a chance to put an end to a two-game absence. Currently, Bam Knight is the only healthy backfield option on Arizona's active roster.

Love maintained his activity level from Wednesday, which followed two weeks off due to a lingering ankle injury. Head coach Mike LaFleur hasn't indicated if Love actually has a chance to return to action Sunday at Dallas, but Friday's practice report will reveal his chances to do so.

Wilson is dealing with sore ribs in the wake of this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, which resulted in a limited session Wednesday and likely will cap his reps one day later. Thursday's injury report will reveal his activity level.

Wingard has been sidelined for the Cardinals' past three games due to a bone bruise in his knee he sustained back in Week 4 against the Giants, and now his availability for Week 8 is in question. If he can upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, there's a good chance he'll suit up Sunday at Dallas.

Wilson's absence Wednesday was marked not injury related, but there does seem to be a knee issue. His activity at practice Thursday and Friday should offer more insight into whether he's truly in danger of sitting out in Week 8.

The transaction comes after Brooks announced earlier in the day that he underwent season-ending wrist surgery. Brooks saw light snaps through the first four weeks of the season, but he stepped in as the Cardinals' No. 3 wideout for the past three games after Marvin Harrison was traded to the Texans. The 26-year-old will finish the 2026 campaign with five receptions for 81 yards on 17 targets to go with 499 yards on 19 kickoff returns.

Reiman hasn't played this season and is currently on the reserve/PUP list. While there haven't been any updates on when the 25-year-old will be back on the field, it appears the door isn't fully closed regarding his return before the end of the 2026 campaign. Reiman has appeared in 21 regular-season games for the Cardinals since being drafted in the third round in the 2024 NFL Draft, amassing nine catches for 55 yards.

It's a typical LaFleur non-answer type of answer. It was reported two weeks ago that Conner was close to practicing, but there's been no indication his 21-day practice window is close to being opened by the Cardinals. There's not much room on the depth chart for another running back that doesn't play special teams in Arizona.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Henderson practiced in full Wednesday. He was downgraded to limited Thursday, popping up on the practice report due to a groin injury that he's dealt with in the last few weeks. With A.J. Terrell (groin) and Avieon Terrell (illness) also in danger of missing the Week 8 meeting with Tampa, Mike Hughes, Mike Ford and Robert Longerbeam may see more action.

Daniels practiced in full Wednesday, though after being downgraded to limited Thursday, there is concern he won't be on the field in Week 8 versus Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old is coming off the best performance of his career in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, garnering 11 tackles (nine solo) and one interception. His services will be needed even more if Divine Deablo (forearm) can't suit up once again. However, if Deablo and Daniels are both sidelined, Harold Perkins, Christian Harris and Josh Woods would likely be more involved.

Deablo injured his forearm during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, which ultimately kept him off the field for Sunday's win over the 49ers. The 28-year-old didn't practice Wednesday, and while he was limited Thursday, he likely has more hurdles to clear before suiting up Sunday versus Tampa Bay. If Deablo can't get out there in Week 8, Harold Perkins and Kendal Daniels (Achilles) could be in line for more snaps.

Zaccheaus didn't play in the 29-20 win over San Francisco on Sunday. While his limited participation in the Falcons' previous two practices is a positive sign, he still may be heading for an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with Tampa Bay. The 29-year-old hasn't been overly involved this season, catching four passes (11 targets) for 17 yards. However, Zaccheaus plays a role as a return man on special teams, so if he's not cleared to play Sunday, Jahan Dotson and Zachariah Branch may see more action in that area, even more so if Brian Robinson (hamstring) is also unavailable.

Robinson has yet to resume practicing after sitting out Atlanta's Week 7 win over the 49ers due to a hamstring injury. Robinson will likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to avoid being ruled out for a second consecutive game, in which case Khalil Herbert would likely be elevated from the practice squad to work as Bijan Robinson's backup again.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Jackson seems on track to return to action for Sunday's game at Buffalo after logging back-to-back uncapped sessions to begin Week 8 prep. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if he's tagged with a designation for that matchup, but the quarterback is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a left high-ankle sprain.

Hawkins has now been held out of four consecutive practices due to the knee issue and could be trending toward missing a second straight game Sunday in Buffalo. If Hawkins ends up being sidelined against the Bills, Keondre Jackson and K'Von Wallace would be in line for extra snaps alongside starting safety Malaki Starks.

Smith may have tweaked his knee during the Ravens' Week 7 loss to the Bengals, when he logged eight tackles (five solo). The veteran linebacker's practice participation over the next two days will determine whether he enters the weekend with an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills.

Randall was a full participant in his return to practice. The Ravens placed the running back on IR in late August with an undisclosed injury, which has now been revealed to be a neck issue. Randall's instant jump to full participation means the fifth-round rookie could be ready to suit up as soon as Sunday's game against the Bills.

Hamilton was spotted walking off the field with a brace on his right knee during Wednesday's session, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic, and the fifth-year defensive back may have picked up the injury during the Ravens' Week 7 loss to the Bengals. Hamilton will have two more opportunities to return to practice in at least a limited capacity before Sunday's game against the Bills.

Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury during the Ravens' Week 6 loss to the Browns. The outside linebacker will spend the rest of 2026 on IR, allowing the Ravens to carry more depth on the offensive line. The team signed offensive guard Kyle Hergel from the practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move.

Tampa was placed on IR in mid-September due to what was diagnosed at the time as a knee injury, but Wednesday's practice report listed ankle and toe injuries for the third-year defensive back. He was a limited participant in his return, and he'll need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's AFC North tilt against the Bengals. Tampa's return would give the Ravens extra depth in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Kincaid has started Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practice sessions coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. The 27-year-old TE has yet to miss a game this season, but Kincaid has cooled down significantly after a scorching start, mustering 90 receiving yards over the past four games after posting 225 yards and a TD through Week 2. Kincaid will look to get back on track Sunday against the Ravens, assuming he plays through the chest injury that's limiting his practice participation.

Moore has been listed as limited both Wednesday and Thursday while practicing in a non-contact jersey. The 29-year-old wide receiver missed Buffalo's last two games prior to a Week 7 bye after having appeared in 92 consecutive regular-season games. Keon Coleman stepped up in Moore's absence and could maintain a larger role Sunday against the Ravens if Moore is ultimately sidelined or limited.

Davis received the day off while he was feeling under the weather, but so long as he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, he should avoid taking a designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens. While handling a backup role behind lead back James Cook this season, Davis has carried just five times for 12 yards to go with three receptions for 40 yards through Buffalo's first six contests.

Shavers has progressed enough in his recovery from a torn ACL to return to practice, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Shavers saw his role in the Bills' offense steadily increase over the course of the 2025 season before suffering his injury in the wild-card round against the Jaguars in January. His next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Brown will be forced to miss Week 8 as he nurses an apparent hand injury. In his absence, Aaron Hall and TeRah Edwards are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Carolina's defensive line.

Simpkins was unable to practice all week due to an ankle injury, which he likely picked up during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers. With Damien Lewis (knee) also ruled out, Corey Bullock will likely start at left guard in Thursday night's game. Simpkins' next chance to suit up is Week 9 against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Lewis likely picked up the injury during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers. He was unable to practice all week due to his injury, and with Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) also ruled out, Corey Bullock figures to step into the starting role at left guard. Lewis' next chance to play is Week 9 against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Evans logged three consecutive DNPs in Week 8 prep. The cornerback was unable to overcome his new injury during the Panthers' short week, leaving him sidelined for Thursday's contest. Will Lee and Chau Smith-Wade are now the only cornerbacks on the Panthers' active roster, meaning multiple defensive backs will likely be elevated to the active roster for Thursday's game.

Phillips did not practice at all during the Panthers' Week 8 prep. The linebacker aggravated a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Eagles and continues to pay the price. It is unclear whether Phillips is tracking to return to practice ahead of Week 9 or will need to miss even more time due to the injury.

Moton fractured his fibula in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. The offensive tackle will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season due to the injury, making the move to injured reserve a formality. Monroe Freeling is set to start at right tackle for the Panthers for the remainder of the season.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Monangai hasn't suited up since Week 4, and he continues to be bothered by a pair of injures at the start of Chicago's Week 8 prep. He'll have an extra day to recover with the Bears playing on MNF against Seattle. Roschon Johnson has played in a change-of-pace role behind D'Andre Swift during Monangai's absence.

Johnson said that Bryant's timeline for return is still indefinite, but it looks like a possibility he could be back on the field as soon as December or January. He is recovering from a knee surgery he underwent back in August after he suffered a hyperextension during training camp. Per Cronin, he is still on a four- to six-month timeline to return.

Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday. Even with the emergence of Colston Loveland, Kmet was still a key piece in Chicago's offense as a run blocker, and he'll end his 2026 regular season with a 10-87-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) across seven games. Rookie third-rounder Sam Roush is the only other healthy tight end on the 53-man roster other than Loveland, so the Bears could look to bolster the position group by trade or free agency.

Muhammad is dealing with a toe injury, and he will now likely be forced to watch the remainder of the game from the Bears' sideline. In Muhammad's absence, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips are both candidates to see an increase in workload at cornerback.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

Dugger was injured in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens and did not return. The 30-year-old will now miss at least one game, and while there will likely be more updates on his health moving forward, he should be considered week-to-week. Dugger hasn't seen consistent action on the defensive side of the ball, though his absence will be felt on special teams.

Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Howard is in the league's concussion protocol after exiting Sunday's win over the Titans due to a concussion. Dawand Jones is in line to start at right tackle if Howard is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Sunday's matchup versus the Steelers.

Hall has missed the Browns' past three games because of a lingering ankle injury, and now his status for Week 8 is in jeopardy. He'll likely need to practice in full Thursday or Friday to not go into the weekend with an injury designation.

Harden hurt his hamstring during Sunday's game at Tennessee, and now his availability for Week 8 is in question. He'll probably have to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram, coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that he gave Verse the day off and expects him to play Sunday at Pittsburgh. With that said, his activity at practice Thursday and Friday might still be worth keeping an eye on.

Schwesinger finished third on the Browns in tackles Sunday behind both Quincy Williams and Ronnie Hickman (10 each). Schwesinger has played every single defensive snap through seven regular-season games and has logged at least eight stops in six of those contests. He's up to 64 total tackles on the year, which leads the Browns and is sixth-most in the NFL.

Davis injured his quad during training camp in late July and started the regular season on IR. His 21-day window opened Oct. 6, but he has not progressed enough in his recovery to warrant his removal from IR. That means that the 2022 sixth-rounder will be sidelined for the rest of the season unless he reaches an injury settlement with the Browns.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Pickens is dealing with a lingering shoulder issue and a new hamstring injury, which so far has capped his practice reps this week. He'll have one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

Williams is dealing with a hamstring injury he likely sustained in the Cowboys' Week 7 win over the Eagles on Monday. The defensive lineman will probably need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

Downs likely suffered his ankle injury in the Cowboys' Week 7 win over the Eagles on Monday. The defensive back's ability to practice, even in a limited fashion in the walkthrough, just two days after sustaining the injury means he will likely be capable of suiting up for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals.

Winters remains sidelined with a calf injury he sustained in the Cowboys' Week 6 loss to the Packers. If the inside linebacker cannot upgrade to at least a limited participant by Friday's practice, he will likely be ruled out ahead of the Week 8 showdown with the Cardinals.

Turpin continues to miss practice with a rib injury he picked up in the Cowboys' Week 6 loss to the Packers. If the team's main returner continues to miss sessions, Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo should continue to return kicks in Week 8 against the Cardinals.

Locke's 21-day practice window opened Friday, and he was a limited participant in each of the last two practices of Week 7 prep. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a foot injury, but he's not quite ready to be activated from IR. His next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Liufau was designated to return from injured reserve Thursday and was a full practice participant Friday and Saturday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag, but the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery from a broken left forearm. Given his ability to practice without restrictions, Liufau has a good chance of being activated from IR for Week 8 against the Cardinals on Nov. 1.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Waddle departed in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's win at Arizona due to a chest injury, which limited him in practice last Wednesday and Thursday before he returned to a full session Friday and didn't enter the weekend with a designation. This week has been a different story, though, as he kicked it off with a DNP on Wednesday before Thursday's capped session. Friday's injury report will reveal Waddle's chances to suit up Sunday against the Chiefs.

Harvey wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, and it's unclear if his limitations a day later stemmed from Denver's initial practice or were the result of an issue the running back encountered Thursday. In any case, added context with regard to Harvey's status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will arrive no later than Friday. If available this weekend, Harvey will contend with J.K. Dobbinsand Jonah Coleman for Denver's Week 8 backfield touches.

Allen sustained the injury late in the second half, and more information on the severity will likely be provided in the near future. The defensive lineman's status at the team's first practice of the week Wednesday will shed more light on his availability  moving forward.

Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

Elliss was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals due to an ankle injury, which is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. He'll be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. The Broncos will get some pass-rushing reinforcement after Jonathon Cooper was activated from the commissioner's exempt list.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Joseph opened the regular season on the reserve/PUP list due to a knee injury that he suffered in Week 6 of the 2025 season. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was limited in Wednesday's session, and there's a chance that he's activated from the PUP list before Sunday's NFC North tilt against the Vikings. The addition of Joseph would bolster a Lions secondary that welcomed back Brian Branch, who picked off Jordan Love in Detroit's Week 7 win over Green Bay.

Coach Dan Campbell said Rakestraw could practice this week, and he has a chance to a play Sunday against the undefeated Vikings. Rock Ya-Sin filled in at cornerback following Rakestraw's injury and would be in line for increased snaps on defense if the latter is unable to face Minnesota.

Bartch has already missed three games due to a foot injury that he sustained against the Bills in Week 2. While on IR, he'll be forced to miss at least four games, so Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 22, is the earliest he can return.

White was diagnosed with a broken forearm following the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. He'll be required to miss at least the next four games on IR, and while he's likely to be sidelined past that minimum window, there's optimism that the veteran linebacker will return at some point this season. Malcolm Rodriguez is the next man up at linebacker in White's absence.

Kennedy suffered a season-ending MCL injury in his right knee during the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. His move to IR opens a spot on Detroit's 53-man roster, and in his absence, Jacob Saylors is in line to take over return duties on kickoffs and punts.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Parsons has spent all season on the PUP list while he continues to recover from the torn ACL he sustained Dec. 14, 2025. Though the Packers haven't relayed that Parsons has experienced any setbacks in his rehab, the team has taken a deliberate approach with easing him back on to the field. After a Thursday game against the Panthers, the Packers will benefit from an extended break leading up to their Week 9 matchup with the Patriots on Nov. 8, which could represent a good opportunity for the team to open Parsons' 21-day evaluation window. Even if Parsons begins practicing next week, he'll still likely face an uphill battle to suit up against New England.

A fifth-round pick in 2024, Monk started the first three games of the season at right guard and was called upon to man center Sunday against the Lions after Sean Rhyan exited with an ankle injury. With Rhyan out multiple weeks and Monk slated to miss at least four games, the Packers will likely turn to John Williams at center after he came on to play the first 58 offensive snaps of his career against Detroit on Sunday.

Houston Texans.longComment: Noel was forced out of this past Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants after going down with the toe injury with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The loss of Noel is a major blow to the Texans, as he had been serving as the team's top return man in addition to emerging as a big-play threat on offense. Through Houston's first seven games, Noel had recorded 19 receptions for a team-leading 331 yards and two touchdowns and added 26 yards on four carries.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Warren has now logged limited practices on back-to-back days after missing the last two games, a positive sign for his progress ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Despite the two-game absence, Warren still leads the Colts with 30 catches and is second on the team behind Jonathan Taylor with three total touchdowns in five appearances. Warren would likely need to log a full practice Friday to avoid an injury designation.

Ogletree presumably picked up the knee injury during Sunday's game at Minnesota, but his status indicates it's probably not too severe. If he can practice in full Thursday or Friday, he could still avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Indianapolis held only a walkthrough practice Wednesday, but Gould seems to have made some progress in his recovery from the concussion that kept him out in Week 7 at Minnesota. He'll still need to be cleared for return to game action by an independent neurologist before suiting up again, if he hasn't been already.

Taylor-Britt suffered the injury on the first play of the fourth quarter of Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings. It's another blow to the Colts' secondary, given that the team was without Sauce Gardner (calf) during Sunday's game, and fellow defensive back Justin Walley sustained a knee injury during the contest. Taylor-Britt will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken are both in line for more defensive snaps in the absence of Taylor-Britt.

Walley exited the Week 7 meeting with the Vikings in the third quarter and did not return. Until there is a more definitive update on his condition, he should be considered questionable ahead of Sunday's game versus the Jaguars. If Walley can't suit up for that contest, Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) and Kapena Gushiken are candidates for more snaps.

A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Allen wasn't listed on the Jaguars' practice report Wednesday, thus he likely picked up the hamstring issue during practice following the team's Week 7 bye. It's unclear how serious the issue is, so the second-year running back's practice participation level Friday should provide clarity about his likelihood of suiting up in Week 8 against Indianapolis. Allen has handled only one carry through six contests, so an absence would primarily affect Jacksonville's special-teams unit.

Coming out of a bye week, Meyers has had his reps capped in the Jaguars' first two practice sessions of Week 8. The Jaguars haven't indicated that Meyers is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Colts, but if he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, he'll likely head into the weekend without an injury designation.

The Jaguars were hoping that Harrison was undergoing just an arthroscopic procedure, but the surgeons found more damage than originally thought. As such, the 2023 first-rounder will miss the rest of the season, and how he progresses in his recovery over the coming months will determine whether he will be available for the start of the 2027 campaign. Walker Little figures to start at left tackle in Harrison's absence.

The Jaguars had listed Johnson as questionable to return after he left in the second quarter due to the ankle injury, but though he was spotted on the sideline in the second half, he never checked back into the contest. Kaevon Merriweather ended up serving as the primary replacement at safety for Johnson, who will have a Week 7 bye to recover from his injury before potentially returning to action Nov. 1 versus the Colts. Johnson accrued six tackles prior to his departure.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Delane practiced Wednesday, though after missing Thursday's session, he is now listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's divisional clash with the Broncos. The 22-year-old rookie dealt with the issue during training camp, and while he managed to suit up in Week 1 against Denver, he aggravated the injury during the contest and missed the Week 2 overtime victory over the Colts. He has had a sound inaugural campaign, amassing 27 total tackles (17 solo), one interception and five passes defended. If Delane can't play in Week 8, Christian Roland-Wallace and Kristian Fulton would be in line for more playing time.

Rice has put a pair of limited practices under his belt as he works his way back from a hamstring injury that has sidelined him since Week 4, with a knee injury also in the mix to complicate his recovery. If Rice ultimately gets the green light to face the Broncos, he would likely reclaim his customary role as Kansas City's top wide receiver. He would likely need to log a full practice Friday to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game.

Kelce logged a full practice Wednesday, but the tight end's listed limitations a day later make his status for Sunday's game against the Broncos worth monitoring. Kelce was also limited in practice last week, but ended up approaching his team's 20-3 loss to Seattle (in which he caught four of his eight targets for 44 yards) without an injury designation.

Moore has progressed enough through the league's concussion protocol to practice without restrictions Wednesday. However, he needs to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available for Sunday's game against the Broncos.

Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.

Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Since being designated for return from injured reserve Monday, Bech has logged consecutive full practices. Should the wideout maintain that level of activity Friday, he'll have a chance to suit up Sunday against the Jets. For that to happen, Bech will need to come of IR by Saturday. If that transpires, the 2025 second-rounder will have a chance to boost a Las Vegas WR corps that has yielded modest production thus far apart from Tre Tucker.

Johnson is dealing with a stinger issue he suffered during the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams. The linebacker will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice if he wants to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

Thomas picked up a shoulder injury against the Rams in Week 7, although he was cleared to return to the contest and finished with one catch on as many targets for eight yards. He would avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets if he were to practice in full over the next two days.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Harris suffered his hamstring injury in Week 5 against Denver and missed Week 6 ahead of last week's bye. With back-to-back limited practices to open Week 8 prep, Harris has a decent chance of suiting up Sunday against the Rams. In a broken Chargers offense, it's difficult to get excited about anyone on the team for fantasy.

McConkey has back-to-back uncapped practices under his belt this week, but it remains unclear if he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires getting the all-clear from an independent neurologist. Friday's injury report will reveal if he still needs to pass such an exam ahead of Sunday's game versus the Rams.

Harbaugh added that Perryman isn't quite ready to return to practice, and given that the veteran linebacker's 21-day practice window has yet to open, he's probably not available for Sunday's game against the Rams. Perryman landed on IR on Sept. 1 due to an undisclosed injury that he may have picked up toward the tail end of training camp.

It is unclear when Leonard sustained his concussion, as the Chargers were on bye in Week 7. The depth cornerback has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not be able to suit up for full-contact activities until he is cleared by an independent neurologist.

Thompson was active in Week 6 during the Chargers' last game before their bye, but he ended up not playing any snaps, presumably due to the quad injury that kept him out for the prior three contests. Now his availability for Week 8 is in doubt, and he'll probably have to return to practice Thursday or Friday to have any chance to play Sunday against the Rams.

James is a candidate for injured reserve and could be out for some time with a persistent hamstring injury. The star strong safety has also been discussed in trade rumors, as the 0-6 Chargers' season appears to be all but over. Tony Jefferson is set to start at strong safety in Sunday's game against the Rams.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Parkinson has now missed the first two days of Week 8 prep, so his status for Sunday's matchup against the Chargers is looking quite precarious. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to have a chance of suiting up this weekend. Rams QB Matthew Stafford peppered his tight-end corps with 14 targets in Week 7 in the absence of wideout Davante Adams (hamstring), so Parkinson's absence would be felt by the team's offense if he can't play. Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen could be set for a bump in targets if that's the case.

Landman returned to practice as a full participant but has not yet officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. With Landman returning to full practice, the announcement that he is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Chargers should come soon. If Landman is ready to play, Grant Stuard and Shaun Dolac should see less action in Week 8.

McDuffie returns to practice to start Week 8 prep, a strong sign for the cornerback's health after he was listed as questionable for Week 7 despite not practicing at all. The 26-year-old star will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Coach Sean McVay revealed that Ferguson's practice window to return from injured reserve won't open during Week 8 prep. Ferguson has missed the minimum four games while on IR due to an ankle sprain, and for as long as he's sidelined, the Rams will continue to roll with Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen at tight end.

Adams tweaked his hamstring on the Rams' final offensive possession of a Week 6 loss to the Cardinals on Oct. 18, and McVay revealed one day later that the wide receiver had a rupture of the hamstring and required surgery, with the aim to return "a little after" the Rams' Week 11 bye. L.A. seems to be targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which is a shade more than six weeks from the initial injury. In any case, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell will continue to earn the WR reps behind top option Puka Nacua.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee after Week 1 and has been on injured reserve in the meantime. Following McVay's comments, Garrett will miss Sunday's contest against the Chargers, which will mark his seventh consecutive absence. Garrett's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 8, at Washington.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Dulcich was also limited at Wednesday's practice, so the tight end likely needs to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Patriots without an injury designation. Dulcich has been targeted five times in each of his last two contests, a span in which he's logged a 9/123/0 receiving line.

With Washington having now logged limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday, the wideout will look to get back to full participation Friday to clear up any concern about his status heading into Sunday's game against the Patriots. Though he leads the Dolphins in both receptions (26) and receiving yards (289), Washington is coming off a Week 7 outing against the Jets in which he drew a season-low three targets while Miami welcomed back promising rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (2-70-2 receiving line on three targets) from a three-game absence due to an ankle injury.

Proctor played all 65 of the Dolphins' offensive snaps in Week 7, but he suffered a concussion somewhere along the way. He'll now need to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol to return to game action. Until then, 2024 sixth-rounder Jarrett Kingston is a candidate to step up at guard.

Wayne may have picked up the injury during the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, when he played 16 snaps (10 on offense, six on special teams) without showing up on the box score otherwise. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's AFC East showdown against New England. Wayne has not recorded a target in each of his last three outings after turning 12 targets into four catches for 65 yards through the first three games of the regular season as a member of the Texans.

Kacmarek may have picked up the injury during the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, when he logged 34 snaps (29 on offense, five on special teams) without showing up on the box score otherwise. The rookie third-rounder will have two more opportunities to return to practice in at least a limited capacity before Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Brents reported concussion symptoms following the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, per Alain Poupart of SI.com. Brents will have two more opportunities to practice this week, but he would not be eligible to play against the Patriots on Sunday unless he's cleared from the league's concussion protocol by an independent neurologist.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: In the wake of making an early exit from this past Sunday's win against the Colts after aggravating a knee injury, Jones didn't practice Wednesday, so his return to drills one day later generally is a good sign in the midst of Week 8 prep. Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Detroit.

New England Patriots.longComment: Henderson will try to shed his illness and return to practice Friday. If he's unable to practice without limitations Friday, the 2025 second-round pick would likely take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Henderson has struggled to earn playing time in recent weeks, splitting change-of-pace work behind Rhamondre Stevenson with Corey Kiner.

Thursday's injury report confirms earlier reporting from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network that Brown isn't practicing Thursday. According to Rapoport, Brown recently had a knee issue flare up, which has the wide receiver's status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins in doubt. Brown has six catches for 75 yards on 16 targets in two games since returning from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.

Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Jets, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Walter Rouse will take over as the team's starting left tackle Thursday night versus the Bears.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Reid sustained a concussion in Sunday's international game and will not return to the contest. The safety has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist for every step of his return journey.

Donaldson picked up the injury during the first quarter and has been taken to the locker room to undergo more tests on his shoulder injury. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller would be the remaining healthy running backs on the Saints active roster for the rest of Sunday's game if Donaldson is not cleared to return.

New York Giants.longComment: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

Skattebo's explosive run put the Giants within field-goal range before he was subbed out for Devin Singletary, who ran up the middle for a 30-yard score to seal the win on the very next play. Though he told Dan Graziano of ESPN.com after the game that he "felt something" in his hamstring that prompted him to slide down at the end of his run rather than being tackled to the ground, Skattebo doesn't sound like he'll require an MRI and should be ready to play in the Giants' next game Nov. 8 versus the Eagles following a Week 8 bye. After being limited to just six snaps in a Week 6 loss to the Saints following a string of poor outings to begin the campaign, Skattebo stepped back into a lead role out of the backfield in Sunday's victory and delivered his best performance of the season, finishing with 121 total yards and a touchdown on 18 touches.

Edmunds will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn chest muscle, so his placement on injured reserve opens up a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster. Micah McFadden is expected to start at inside linebacker alongside Arvell Reese for the rest of the season in Edmunds' absence, with Jack Kelly and Zaire Barnes providing depth at the position.

New York Jets.longComment: Hall last suited up in Week 3, but back-to-back limited practices suggest that the running back could return to the Jets' lineup Sunday against the Raiders. That said, Hall will likely need to log a full practice Friday in order to approach Week 8 action without an injury designation.

Ossai is unlikely to play in Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders and is currently considered week-to-week due to an ankle injury he sustained during the Week 5 win over the Browns. Will McDonald and Nate Lynn should continue to see increased playing time in Ossai's absence.

Bailey sustained injury during Sunday's loss to the Dolphins but was able to finish the game, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Bailey will be evaluated throughout the week before the team determines his availability for this Sunday's matchup with the Raiders. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Bailey leads all rookies with 5.5 sacks and is tied with Carl Granderson, Elijah Ponder and T.J. Watt for fifth-most in the NFL.

Sweat did not participate in Wednesday's practice as he continues to deal with the knee injury he sustained in the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The defensive tackle will likely miss Week 8 against the Raiders and could miss even longer due to the new injury.

Mauigoa suited up for the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots before being ruled out for Week 7 against the Browns. The linebacker has missed three regular-season games so far in 2026 and will need to miss at least four more while on IR.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Smith so far has sat out Wednesday's walkthrough and Thursday's practice due to a lingering hamstring injury, giving him just one more opportunity to mix into drills this week. The Eagles may make a ruling on Smith's status for Sunday's game in Washington once they post their final Week 8 injury report Friday.

Barkley has yet to practice this week due to dueling hamstring and back issues, the latter of which knocked him out of Monday's loss to the Cowboys. He relayed to Tim McManus of ESPN.com afterward that he isn't concerned about the most recent injury, but he now has just one more chance to get back on the practice field ahead of Sunday's game at Washington. With all of Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) on IR, Jaydon Blue currently is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though the team also used practice squad member Elijah Mitchell in Monday's loss to the Cowboys.

Wicks hasn't practiced in any fashion since Week 6 while he continues to manage an ankle injury. Unless he's able to get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Wicks will likely be ruled out for a second straight game this Sunday at Washington.

Smith entered the league's concussion protocol against the Panthers in Week 6. He did not practice during Week 7 prep, so his limited status Wednesday indicates that he is progressing in his recovery. He would need to be cleared from the league's protocol by an independent neurologist in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

Wednesday was the first time Carter would have practiced since sustaining an abdominal injury in Week 5 against the Jaguars. He'll have two more opportunities to log a full practice, which would likely be enough for him to be cleared to return from a two-game absence and play in Sunday's game against the Commanders.

Campbell likely picked up the injuries during the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday, when he logged two assisted tackles while playing 41 snaps (37 on defense, four on special teams). He has two more chances to return to practice this week, although he could be tagged with an injury designation for Sunday's NFC East tilt against the Commanders depending on his participation levels.

Pierce thus is joining fellow RBs Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) on IR, leaving Saquon Barkley and Jaydon Blue as the only players at the position on the Eagles' active roster. Pierce made a late exit from Monday's loss to the Cowboys, which followed Barkley's own earlier departure due to a back issue. Pierce's health concern is enough for him to miss at least four contests, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, in Arizona.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Skowronek has missed the Steelers' last two games with a calf injury he sustained back in Week 5 versus the Colts, and now his availability for Week 8 is up in the air. Whether he ends up suiting up Sunday versus the Browns might hinge on whether he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday.

Joseph-Day is dealing with an apparent triceps injury, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Gabriel Rubio and Kevin Jobity are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Pittsburgh's defensive line.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout was only going to enter the game in an emergency scenario for the 49ers' secondary. The team hopes the Week 8 bye will allow Stout's shoulder sprain to fully heal ahead of the Week 9 showdown with the Raiders.

A lingering knee injury has sidelined Bosa for each of the 49ers' last five games. He has yet to return to practice, but with San Francisco getting extra rest thanks to the bye, the veteran pass rusher could be available for Week 9. Bosa's return would result in less snaps being available on the edge for the likes of Romello Height, Mykel Williams, Ogbo Okoronkwo and Khalid Kareem.

All three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Samuel and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) are eyeing a Week 9 return against the Raiders, so the 49ers' wide receiver depth chart could look vastly different coming out of the bye. Samuel would likely go back to his part-time role, handling short-area passes and an occasional handoff or two. He's not a particularly exciting fantasy play when Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) are all healthy.

Shanahan said the same thing 11 days ago, so the timeline appears to remain in place for Robinson, who suffered a high-ankle sprain way back in Week 2 against Miami. The Niners are expected to get plenty of reinforcements following their open date, and all three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Robinson could be among those returning for Week 9 against Las Vegas.

Stribling was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and remains on injured reserve. He missed a big opportunity for snaps and targets with the team dealing with so many injuries at the wide receiver position, but all indications are Stribling will be back for the stretch run and a possible trip to the playoffs.

After missing Sunday's game against the Falcons with the Achilles issue, Evans appears to be trending toward a return for San Francisco's next contest in Week 9 against the Raiders. Working as the Niners' big-play X receiver this season, Evans has been nearly unstoppable when healthy. Maintaining health has been his biggest issue. When on the field, Evans is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside.

After McCaffrey briefly exited Sunday's loss to Atlanta with what had been described as a thigh issue, this update offers more clarity on the injury and a favorable outlook. The timing of the 49ers' bye gives the veteran running back added recovery time ahead of their next game in Week 9 versus the Raiders, though his practice status will still be worth monitoring once San Francisco returns to work. Kaelon Black will be a priority add off waivers considering CMC's injury history.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Shaheed was injured in last Sunday night's win over the Chiefs, but indications are he avoided a serious injury. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Bears, Tory Horton will slot into WR3 duties behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.

It was Price's first practice after being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Thursday, which opened the rookie running back's 21-day window for activation. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) potentially set to debut Monday night against the Bears and the presence of both Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, it's difficult to see any of these running backs being reliable fantasy options until/unless the Seahawks pare this backfield down.

Going back to last week, Charbonnet now has logged four straight full sessions, indicating that he's drawing closer to his first game action since tearing his left ACL on Jan. 17. Of course, the Seahawks didn't clear him to return this past Sunday against the Chiefs, and rookie first-round RB Jadarian Price (chest) was limited Thursday after the Seahawks designated him for return from IR, throwing another question mark into the potential backfield for Week 8. In any case, Charbonnet will have two more chances to prove his health before Seattle makes a ruling on his status ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

Cross suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Chiefs. While an official return date hasn't been established, there is hope he can get back on the field in "one or two weeks." With Cross on the shelf, Josh Jones is the favorite to start in Week 8 versus Chicago and beyond.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Though Egbuka was limited again, he shed the non-contact jersey and worked in a normal practice jersey Thursday. He was still dialed back enough to be listed as limited, but he seems to be making progress as Sunday approaches. Egbuka is working back from a concussion and a foot injury after missing Week 7.

Gainwell returned to practice after sitting out Wednesday's session, but he still faced some limitations Thursday. He'll have one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Friday, and if Gainwell is able to do so, he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Bucky Irving remains atop Tampa Bay's depth chart at running back, followed by Gainwell and Sean Tucker.

Hayes underwent a minor procedure on his knee after getting hurt in the preseason, and there's currently no timetable for his return following the setback. Once healthy, the 27-year-old should contribute on special teams.

Rozeboom will be forced to miss at least four games while recovering from a finger injury that he likely suffered in Week 6 against the Steelers. In his absence, SirVocea Dennis will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker behind starters Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: The same applies applies to Wednesday's session, giving the wideout one more chance to up his participation level ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals. So far this season, Ridley has recorded just five catches on 10 targets for 81 yards in six games, a pace that has kept him off the fantasy radar thus far.

Spears is sitting out a second consecutive practice, which doesn't bode well for his availability Sunday against the Bengals considering he was unable to suit up for the Week 7 loss to Cleveland. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to avoid being ruled out on the Titans' subsequent injury report.

Tate also sat out Wednesday due to this injury. The rookie fourth overall pick will have one more opportunity to practice in some capacity Friday ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals. If Tate sits out a game for the first time in his young career, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley (hip) could get more downfield targets while Wan'Dale Robinson runs his customary short and intermediate routes.

Townsend went down with the injury when a teammate was pushed into him during his punt with 1:45 remaining in the second quarter. The Titans deemed Townsend questionable to return, and though he was able to check back into the contest to handle holding duties on a field-goal and extra-point attempt in the fourth quarter, placekicker Joey Slye stepped in for the Titans' lone punt of the second half. Tennessee could look to work out multiple punters over the next couple of days and potentially sign one if Townsend's availability for a Week 8 matchup with the Bengals is in any peril.

Tennessee placed Mausi on injured reserve at the conclusion of the preseason due to a previously unspecified injury, but the team's first Week 7 injury report revealed that he's been working his way back from a foot issue. Mausi was able to turn in a full practice Wednesday, potentially giving him a shot at playing as soon as this Sunday versus the Browns if the Titans are willing to bring him back from IR.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Burks was limited in Wednesday's practice, and it's unclear if his 'DNP' a day later was maintenance-related or the result of a setback. If Burks is available Sunday against the Eagles, he'll have an opportunity to make an impact in a Washington WR corps that has lost receiving yardage leader Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury.

Bates has been a spectator for the Commanders' first two Week 8 practices and will need to get back on the field in some capacity to put himself in position to play Sunday against the Eagles. The sixth-year tight end has played at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Commanders' first six games, mainly serving as a blocking specialist while recording five receptions for 27 yards on six targets.

Tunsil has another check-up in a few weeks, which will give the Commanders a better sense of a potential return timeline in 2026. The offensive tackle is still a ways away from football, but the consistency in his recovery process leaves the door open for an eventual return.

Kinlaw injured his knee during the first half of the Commanders' Week 6 loss against the 49ers. He had additional time to recover thanks to the Week 7 bye, but it looks like the veteran defensive lineman will not play in Sunday's NFC East tilt. Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle), Shy Tuttle and Deatrich Wise would all be in line for more defensive snaps if Kinlaw is indeed ruled out.

Newton underwent surgery for a torn pectoral back in August, but it now looks like he's close to being fully recovered. His activity at practice during the week will be worth keeping an eye on as Washington prepares for a Week 8 contest versus the Eagles.

McLaurin's move to IR was merely a formality, as the 31-year-old wideout was recently diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee that will require season-ending surgery. The transaction clears a spot on the 53-man roster for fellow wideout Van Jefferson, whom the Commanders signed off their practice squad.

Lane sustained his season-ending ankle injury during the Commanders' Week 4 win against the Colts, and the injury was severe enough for him to stay in London overnight to be monitored and undergo additional tests. His absence has opened the door to more playing time for both Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, and they are both candidates for another bump in playing time after Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.
